title: Implement windowing to avoid render elements not on the screen
body:
Let's do a POC at implementing lazyload: true on the hits widget, it should then only render react hits elements when they are visible, with an offset (so that if you start scrolling, you already see some).

Multiple libraries are already either doing windowing or tracking dom nodes position inside the window. Let's try to use them.

comments.body:
I managed to do that on several demos already, using your `inviewport` library. It still requires a bit of hacky code (until https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/issues/903 is fixed. I'll submit a PR to take care of that).

I'm not sure this is something we should include in the core (it requires an external lib, and will need a few options to configure). Maybe I could just write a guide about how to implement that?

> Let's do a POC at implementing lazyload: true on the hits widget, it should then only render react hits elements when they are visible, with an offset (so that if you start scrolling, you already see some).

Did we feel the pain somehow? I've the feeling that except when you have a crazy amount of big/non-appropriated pictures per  page, you never need such optimization - even if we're talking about dozens of hits - that should be super fast.
20 images in ecommerce product format + mobile 3g/ adsl and you should feel the pain.
That, and when you're using cloudinary and don't want to hit your quota too quickly. This was also requested by SteamDB.

I think that for now what we would need is a guide on how to implement lazyloading on the hits widget, no need for a generic API entry.

Moved to #1072
